notes:
PRIMARY review of sanitizeTrackingParams + sanitizeTrackingValue (app/javascript/shared/lib/utils.js:23-88), traced against the two callers (AuthForm.tsx:41 and SignupForm.tsx:26, both pass a real location.search — always a string, leading '?' or ''), SPEC.md §5.1 + §252, and the actual library sources in node_modules. NO DEFECTS FOUND. Detail:

(1) OCCURRENCE ORDER — the crux (failure-pattern #28). Confirmed query-string is v6.1.0 (node_modules/query-string/package.json). Read node_modules/query-string/index.js: parse() ends in `return Object.keys(ret).sort().reduce(...)` — keys are alphabetized UNCONDITIONALLY, no opt-out in this version. The code correctly derives ORDER from the raw string via queryString.extract(search).split('&') (utils.js:46-56) and reads VALUES from queryString.parse (utils.js:43). ORDER from raw string, VALUES from parse — exactly right.

(2) ARRAY-VALUE ORDER survives the sort. In parse(), the final reduce calls keysSorter(value) only when `typeof value === 'object' && !Array.isArray(value)`; for repeated-param arrays the `!Array.isArray` guard is false, so `result[key] = value` keeps the array untouched. Arrays are built in occurrence order via `[].concat(accumulator[key], value)` in the default parserForArrayFormat. Therefore sanitizeTrackingValue's `isArray(value) ? value[0] : value` (utils.js:32) yields the FIRST occurrence, matching spec rule 1.

(3) FIRST-10 CAP applies to occurrence-ordered keys. keysInOccurrenceOrder is deduped (indexOf === -1 guard, utils.js:53) so a repeated key holds its FIRST-occurrence position; the utmDataKeys filter (utm_ prefix, excluding utm_source/utm_campaign) preserves that order and .slice(0, UTM_DATA_MAX_KEYS=10) (utils.js:77) takes the first 10 distinct additional utm_* keys. Matches spec rule 3 exactly ('at most 10 utm_* keys beyond utm_source/utm_campaign — the first 10 by occurrence order'). utm_source/utm_campaign are filtered out BEFORE the slice, so they do not consume the 10-key budget — consistent with 'up to 10 ADDITIONAL'.

(4) DECODER MATCH (check #4). Read node_modules/decode-uri-component (v0.2.0) — it is the EXACT same package query-string requires internally (`const decodeComponent = require('decode-uri-component')`). Key derivation is byte-identical between the two: query-string's parse does `param.replace(/\+/g,' ').split('=')[0]` then `decode(key)`=decodeComponent(key); utils.js:51-52 does `param.replace(/\+/g,' ').split('=')[0]` then decodeUriComponent(rawKey). So decodedKey === the key stored in parsedParams, and every parsedParams[decodedKey] lookup resolves. Verified encoded-key equivalence: `?utm%5Fsource=x` decodes to utm_source on BOTH paths (top-level capture succeeds); a repeated encoded/plain key (`utm_medium` + `utm%5Fmedium`) collapses to one deduped key with value[0]=first. MALFORMED %-encoding does NOT throw: decode-uri-component's export tries decodeURIComponent then falls back to customDecodeURIComponent (best-effort) on URIError; it throws only a TypeError on NON-STRING input, and rawKey is always a string from .split('=')[0]. A key that fails strict decode is thus retained (best-effort), not crashed.

(5) sanitizeTrackingValue branches (check #3): repeated -> value[0]; non-string (null from a bare `?utm_source`, or any non-string) -> returned as-is (utils.js:33), matching spec 'A param present with no value parses to null and passes through as-is'; string -> slice(0,255); trailing lone HIGH surrogate (0xD800-0xDBFF) -> slice(0,-1) (utils.js:37-38). slice(0,-1) drops exactly the last code unit — no off-by-one. Empty-string safety: charCodeAt(-1) on '' returns NaN, NaN>=0xd800 is false, returns '' — no crash. The high-surrogate-only handling matches spec rule 2 verbatim (rule 2 scopes the drop to the slice-splitting case, which can only orphan a HIGH surrogate; a trailing lone LOW surrogate is not slice-induced and is unreachable from URL-decoded input). Surrogate semantics were already reviewed and fixed in qa-run-2 Layer-2 (l2-B1, commit fa51c91a5) — not re-litigated.

(6) EDGE CASES walked, all correct: search='' -> parse {} + extract('')='' -> keysInOccurrenceOrder=[] -> returns {}; search='?' -> both empty -> {}; search='?&' -> parsedParams={'':null}, occurrence keys skipped (length 0), '' does not match utm_ prefix -> {}; a param with no '=' -> value null, passes through; bare '&' segments -> skipped by `if (param.length === 0) return`; utm_ boundary — `utm_` exact matches indexOf('utm_')===0 (harmless), `utmx` does NOT (utm_ is not a substring), `utm_source`/`utm_campaign` excluded by name from utmData; value undefined vs '' distinguished (undefined => key absent, '' => empty string kept).

(6b) RULE 13 (no fabricated fallbacks): top-level keys added only under `parsedParams.X !== undefined` guards (utils.js:59,62,65) and utmData keys under `parsedParams[key] !== undefined` (utils.js:75); utmData object itself created only when utmDataKeys.length > 0 (utils.js:79) — no `|| ''`, `|| {}`, or `|| 0`. Matches spec §177 absence semantics. Prototype-pollution safe: parsedParams is Object.create(null); utmData only ever receives utm_-prefixed literal keys (e.g. a `utm___proto__` param sets the literal property 'utm___proto__', not '__proto__'), and __proto__/constructor keys never match the utm_ prefix or the three literal top-level names.

NOT RE-FLAGGED (per SETTLED list in brief/QA-MED-FINDINGS): decode-uri-component v0.2.0 phantom-dependency + its CVE; sanitizer throw on non-string / '?'-less input unreachable from callers (both callers pass real location.search); key-length uncapped; utils.test.js deliberately absent. Cross-checked all against spec §5.1 rules 1-3, §170, §174-177, §252 — full conformance.
